title: Leaving Jack Carey to lead his own band and sorting the chronology
summary: Pushed by sidemen to start his own band; E.D. Morris came in on trombone; the order of Ernest Johnson, Carey, Celestin is worked out.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Let me see. I bought John Jack in 20.

And I would have stayed with him all the time. And I would have stayed with him all the time. But Joy Boyer, Walter Preston, Joe Gable, Chani Foster. And them guys kept forcing me to quit Jack and let's get us own band. They did that a long time before I quit. But I said, well all right, I said we're going to put the band in your name. Kept on- I didn't want to quit Jack. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. They just kept forcing me to quit Jack and let's get us our own band. They did that a long time before I quit. But I said, well all right, we're going to put the band in your name. I didn't want to quit Jack, but they did and so I just went on to quit. But we didn't ever fall out. So I got my own band. And we did good. But I wouldn't think about doing anything like that myself.
Why did they want to quit Jack?
I don't know myself, but I guess they just figured if we, I don't know, there wasn't nothing wrong with him. I don't know. I didn't see nothing wrong.
Well now, when you quit Jack Carey, who came in on trombone with your band?
E.D. Morris. Right on. I'm right in. I see. I said, George Boyd went and got him right away.
And that would be around the time you were playing with Celestan then, huh?

I don't know how it mixed up, but I wasn't with Celestan then. I must have been with Celestan in 19 and going into 20, see. Because I went with Jack Carey from, I don't know how that thing messed up now. Yeah. From, I can't see because I left in 27. That's what got me positive.
Well you had your own band up until the time you left. That's right.
So it had to be Jack Carey before your band.
And then Celestan must have been before that.
No, yeah, yeah, yeah, because Ernest Johnson was the first one. But I didn't play with Ernest Johnson for more than two or three months.
I didn't stay there long at all.
And Jack Carey heard you though while you were with Ernest Johnson.
